title: Question 14728
subject: Criminal Law & Procedure
stem:
Lydia was babysitting 11-year-old Timothy one evening while Timothy’s parents were at a prayer meeting. Lydia noticed that Peter, the next-door neighbor, had left his apartment but that the door had not closed completely behind him.

Lydia said to Timothy, “Let’s play a Bible-quest game. Go next door and see if you can find my portable Bible-story projector, which I lent to Peter, and bring it back here.”

Lydia knew that the projector belonged to Peter and planned to keep it for herself. Timothy believed the projector belonged to Lydia. He went next door, found the projector, and carried it out the front door. At that moment, Peter returned and found Timothy in the hallway with the projector. Timothy explained the “game.” Peter took back his projector and called the police.

Lydia is

choices.A: not guilty of larceny or attempted larceny, because Timothy did not commit any crime.
choices.B: not guilty of larceny but guilty of attempted larceny, because Lydia never acquired possession of the projector.
choices.C: guilty of larceny as an accessory to Timothy.
choices.D: guilty of larceny by the use of an innocent agent.

rightExplanation:
D is correct.

Gold Key: When a person with the required criminal intent causes an innocent person to do the physical act, the guilty person can be treated as committing the offense through an innocent agent. The innocent person’s lack of mens rea does not erase the guilty person’s liability.

Silver Key: When the answer choices form a role-label ladder — no crime, attempt, accessory, innocent agent — ask two facts only: who had the guilty mind, and whose hand moved the property?

Here, Lydia had the guilty mind. Timothy supplied the physical movement of the projector, but he thought it belonged to Lydia. Timothy’s innocence is not a shield for Lydia. Lydia used Timothy as the hand that carried out her taking. The completed carrying away occurred when Timothy carried Peter’s projector out the front door.
studentScript: Timothy is innocent, but Timothy is not the call. Lydia had the steal-intent and used Timothy as the hand. Timothy carried the projector out. Completed larceny through innocent agent. Pick D.

A.signal: The answer stops at Timothy’s innocence and treats it as dispositive of Lydia’s liability.
A.lawyer: Timothy’s innocence does not bar Lydia’s liability when Lydia caused Timothy to carry out the taking with Lydia’s larcenous intent.

B.signal: The answer proves Lydia never personally possessed the projector, but the call asks whether she is liable for the taking through Timothy.
B.lawyer: Physical possession by Lydia is not required if she is legally accountable for Timothy’s act as an innocent agent.

C.signal: Accessory language is from the right neighborhood, but Timothy is not the guilty principal.
C.lawyer: Because Timothy lacked larcenous intent, Lydia is not best described as an accessory to Timothy; she is liable as the principal through an innocent agent.

D.signal: This choice names the role-label that matches the two load-bearing facts: Lydia had the guilty mind; Timothy supplied the innocent hand.
D.lawyer: D matches the innocent-agent rule and the completed taking/carrying away.

goldKeys.statement: A person with the required mens rea who causes an innocent person to perform the criminal act can be guilty as the principal through an innocent agent.
goldKeys.trigger: Adult lies to a child or innocent actor, the innocent actor moves the property, and the adult plans to keep it.
goldKeys.unlocks: Defeats the no-crime, attempt-only, and accessory-label traps.
goldKeys.authority: Model Penal Code § 2.06(2)(a); common-law innocent-agent principle.

silverKeys.statement: When the choices are no crime, attempt, accessory, and innocent agent, ask: who had the guilty mind, and whose hand moved the property?
silverKeys.trigger: A nonculpable immediate actor plus a culpable planner.

remediation.title: Guilty mind, innocent hand
remediation.signal: A child or mistaken person physically performs the taking.
remediation.studentMove: Do not stop at the immediate actor’s innocence. Route the guilty mind through the innocent hand.
remediation.tinyRule: Innocent actor does not block liability for the person who caused the act with the required mens rea.
